_comment: Stories told about random events (user's request, 2026-10-10; ui-spec.md component 25 neighbourhood, design.md 2.7). Each story belongs to one event kind; a player sees none twice until every story of its kind has run. Ids are stored in turn reports: never rename or reuse one. Text fits both agencies and carries no figures (the report adds the event's own line). A story with "requiresGoal" waits until the agency has reached that goal (2026-10-27: no hardware overhead before a satellite in orbit); the goal must exist in every pack. Placeholders: {name} (the person an event struck), {component} (RELIABILITY_SETBACK), {group} (MORALE_BOOST, MORALE_DROP). Counts per kind: EventStories.SIZED, held by EventStoriesTest.

stories.headline: Sacks of letters from schoolchildren
stories.text: A children's magazine asks its readers to write to the agency. The post office delivers the replies by the truckload, and the papers print the best drawings.

stories.headline: A documentary fills the cinemas
stories.text: A short film about the agency's work runs before the main feature in every cinema in the country. Audiences stay in their seats to applaud.

stories.headline: Queues at the world's fair
stories.text: The agency's pavilion at an international exhibition draws the longest queues of the fair. Foreign visitors leave with model rockets and a good impression.

stories.headline: A science prize for the tracking team
stories.text: An academy of sciences honours the agency's tracking engineers for a new way of fixing a spacecraft's position. The award ceremony is broadcast nationwide.

stories.headline: On the cover of every magazine
stories.text: A weekly magazine runs a long feature on the agency, and others follow within days. Newsagents report the issues selling out.

stories.headline: Radio amateurs join in
stories.text: Radio clubs across the country start listening for the agency's signals and sending in their logs. The agency thanks them on air, and membership doubles.

stories.headline: A foreign delegation is impressed
stories.text: Visiting scientists tour the agency's test stands and say so in their own papers back home. The quotes are reprinted here the next morning.

stories.headline: A rocket in the national parade
stories.text: A full-size mock-up of the agency's rocket rolls down the capital's main avenue on parade day. It gets the loudest cheer of the afternoon.

stories.headline: Into the school textbooks
stories.text: The education ministry adds a chapter on spaceflight to next year's textbooks, illustrated with the agency's own photographs.

stories.headline: Open day draws a crowd
stories.text: The agency opens its gates to the public for a day. Families picnic beside the launch towers, and the roads are jammed until midnight.

stories.headline: A song about the stars
stories.text: A song about the agency's rocket crews tops the radio charts. Dance halls play it three times a night.

stories.headline: Watching the sky together
stories.text: Newspapers print the times to spot the agency's hardware passing overhead. Whole towns turn off their street lights to watch.

stories.headline: A glowing editorial
stories.text: The country's most serious newspaper, usually sparing with praise, calls the agency the best-run project in the land.

stories.headline: Lecture halls overflow
stories.text: Agency engineers give a series of public lectures at the university. Students sit on the stairs and in the corridors to hear them.

stories.headline: Pictures of the clouds from above
stories.text: Photographs taken from high altitude show a storm system whole for the first time. Weather forecasters call them a gift.

stories.headline: A stamp for the agency
stories.text: The post office issues a stamp showing the agency's emblem against the stars. The first-day covers are gone by noon.

stories.headline: Every child wants a rocket
stories.text: Toy makers cannot keep up with orders for tin rockets and space helmets. The shop windows are full of the agency's colours.

stories.headline: Praise from the head of state
stories.text: In a speech on the anniversary of the nation's founding, the head of state singles out the agency as the country's pride.

stories.headline: A new computer arrives
stories.text: A room-sized computer is installed in the engineering building. Calculations that took a team of mathematicians a week now take an afternoon.

stories.headline: The wind tunnel is finished
stories.text: The new high-speed wind tunnel runs its first tests. Engineers can now try a shape in the morning and change it by evening.

stories.headline: A partnership with the university
stories.text: The polytechnic lends the agency its best graduate students and its metallurgy laboratory. The engineers wonder how they managed without them.

stories.headline: A lighter, stronger alloy
stories.text: A supplier delivers a new aluminium alloy that keeps its strength when hot. Parts that kept failing on the test stand now hold.

stories.headline: A second test stand opens
stories.text: A second engine test stand goes into service. The test crews no longer wait their turn, and firings run day and night.

stories.headline: Better telemetry
stories.text: New recording equipment captures hundreds of measurements per test instead of a dozen. The engineers finally see what their hardware is doing.

stories.headline: A forgotten report solves a problem
stories.text: A librarian turns up a pre-war research report on combustion instability. It explains a fault the engineers have been chasing for months.

stories.headline: A drive for quality
stories.text: Every worker on the assembly floor learns to sign off their own work and stop the line when something looks wrong. Fewer parts come back from testing.

stories.headline: The clean room opens
stories.text: A dust-free assembly room with filtered air opens for delicate instruments. Valves and gyroscopes stop failing for no reason.

stories.headline: Veterans from the aircraft industry
stories.text: A group of senior aircraft designers joins the agency as advisers. Their rules of thumb save the young engineers from old mistakes.

stories.headline: A tough design review
stories.text: A week-long review tears every drawing apart and puts it back together. The engineers come out tired, and with far fewer open questions.

stories.headline: Precision machine tools
stories.text: New precision lathes and milling machines arrive from abroad. Parts now come out to the tolerance the drawings ask for.

stories.headline: Volunteers for the night shift
stories.text: Inspired by recent events, technicians volunteer for an extra night shift. The workshops never go dark.

stories.headline: An expert on loan
stories.text: A leading specialist in guidance systems is lent to the agency by the defence ministry. Problems that stalled for weeks are settled in days.

stories.headline: The materials laboratory
stories.text: A new laboratory can test how materials behave in vacuum and extreme cold. The engineers stop guessing and start measuring.

stories.headline: Standard parts
stories.text: The design bureaus agree on a common catalogue of bolts, connectors and valves. Each new design no longer starts from scratch.

stories.headline: A class of bright graduates
stories.text: This year's engineering graduates asked for the agency first. The new hires bring fresh mathematics and boundless energy.

stories.headline: A flight simulator for engineers
stories.text: An analogue computer that imitates a rocket in flight goes into use. Engineers can now fly a design many times before building it.

stories.headline: A better fuel contract
stories.text: The agency signs a long contract for rocket propellants at a fixed price. Deliveries come cheaper for a good while.

stories.headline: Sharing the tracking stations
stories.text: The weather service agrees to share its radar stations and staff. The agency stops paying for its own.

stories.headline: A sharp-eyed auditor
stories.text: A new auditor finds the agency paying three suppliers for the same parts. The duplicate contracts are cancelled.

stories.headline: The site gets its own power plant
stories.text: A small power plant comes online at the launch site. Electricity bills that ran the test stands drop sharply.

stories.headline: A railway to the site
stories.text: A new rail spur reaches the assembly halls. Stages and fuel no longer travel the last miles by road.

stories.headline: Surplus equipment for free
stories.text: The armed forces hand over surplus radios, trucks and generators. The agency stops renting its own.

stories.headline: Housing for the staff
stories.text: New apartment blocks near the site are finished. The agency no longer pays for hotel rooms and long bus rides.

stories.headline: Helium recovered
stories.text: A technician designs a way to capture the helium used to pressurise test tanks. Expensive gas that was vented is now reused.

stories.headline: The canteen takes over
stories.text: The site canteen starts feeding the night shifts too. Meal allowances and outside caterers are a thing of the past.

stories.headline: Half the paperwork
stories.text: A review of the agency's forms cuts them by half. A whole floor of clerks moves to work that matters.

stories.headline: Suppliers compete
stories.text: Two factories now make the same valves, and each wants the other's share. Prices fall for a while.

stories.headline: A mild season
stories.text: Gentle weather means no frozen pipes, no snow clearing and little heating. The site's upkeep comes in well under plan.

stories.headline: A celebration for the {group}
stories.text: After a good season the director throws a party in the assembly hall. The {group} dance until the morning shift arrives.

stories.headline: Families visit the site
stories.text: The {group} bring their families to see where they work. Children sit in the control room chairs and ask a hundred questions.

stories.headline: Medals for the {group}
stories.text: The {group} are decorated at a ceremony in the capital. They come back with their medals and a fresh sense of purpose.

stories.headline: A letter of thanks
stories.text: A letter from the head of state thanking the {group} by name is pinned up in the corridor. People stop to read it on their way in.

stories.headline: A club house for the {group}
stories.text: A club house with a library, a billiard table and a small cinema opens for the {group}. Evenings at the site are no longer dull.

stories.headline: Newsreel night
stories.text: A newsreel of the space race is shown to the {group} on a big screen. They cheer every rocket that rises, as if it were their own.

stories.headline: A supplementary budget
stories.text: Impressed by the agency's progress, the government votes the agency a supplementary budget. The money arrives with a request to keep it up.

stories.headline: Money from the defence budget
stories.text: The defence ministry moves part of its own budget to the agency, arguing that the work serves both. Nobody objects.

stories.headline: Industry pays its share
stories.text: Electronics and metals firms agree to fund part of the agency's work in return for the right to use what it learns.

stories.headline: A public subscription
stories.text: A newspaper starts a fund for the space programme. Workers, pensioners and schoolchildren send what they can, and it adds up.

stories.headline: The regions want a piece
stories.text: Provinces hoping for new factories lobby for the agency's budget. Their votes carry a raise for the coming seasons.

stories.headline: A contaminated batch
stories.text: Inspectors find metal shavings in a batch of parts for {component}. Every unit built from it has to be taken apart and checked.

stories.headline: Built to the wrong drawing
stories.text: A workshop has been building {component} parts to an old revision of the drawings. Weeks of testing have to be repeated.

stories.headline: Cracks under the microscope
stories.text: Fatigue cracks turn up in a {component} part that passed every test. The engineers go back to their calculations.

stories.headline: A fire on the test stand
stories.text: A {component} test article catches fire on the stand. Nobody is hurt, but the data from the last run cannot be trusted.

stories.headline: {name} sprains an ankle
stories.text: {name} twists an ankle on the training course and has to sit out the next exercises. Basic training runs a season longer.

stories.headline: {name} retakes an exam
stories.text: {name} narrowly fails the written examination and must retake it with the next class.

stories.headline: No place on the course
stories.text: The course {name} needs next is full. The instructors promise a place in the following session.

stories.headline: {name} fails a security review
stories.text: A routine security review turns up something in {name}'s file. The agency lets them go the same week, and nobody explains why.

stories.headline: {name} dismissed for negligence
stories.text: A safety inspection finds {name} signed off work that was never done. The director dismisses them on the spot.

stories.headline: {name} talks to the press
stories.text: {name} describes unfinished plans to a journalist over dinner. The story runs the next day, and {name} is gone the day after.

stories.headline: {name} fails the medical
stories.text: A late medical check finds a heart murmur in {name}. The doctors will not sign the papers, and {name} leaves.

stories.headline: {name} is not cut out for it
stories.text: The instructors agree that {name} cannot keep up with the course. {name} takes the news calmly and goes home.

stories.headline: {name} fails the final examination
stories.text: {name} fails the final examination twice. The rules allow no third attempt.

stories.headline: {name} takes an industry job
stories.text: An aircraft manufacturer offers {name} twice the salary. {name} hands in their notice with an apology.

stories.headline: {name} goes home
stories.text: With a sick parent far away, {name} resigns to be closer to family. The colleagues hold a small farewell in the canteen.

stories.headline: {name} has had enough
stories.text: After too many nights at the site, {name} resigns. The letter is short and polite.

stories.headline: {name} falls ill
stories.text: A bad case of pneumonia keeps {name} in hospital and then at home to recover.

stories.headline: {name} in a car accident
stories.text: {name}'s car slides off an icy road on the way to the site. Nothing serious, but the doctors order rest.

stories.headline: {name} on loan to a ministry
stories.text: A ministry borrows {name} for an urgent commission of inquiry. The agency has no say in it.

stories.headline: The safety board limits launches
stories.text: After a near miss at another site, the national safety board allows only one launch this turn while it reviews procedures.

stories.headline: The range is shared
stories.text: Military tests take over the range for most of the turn. The agency gets one launch window and no more.

stories.headline: Only one pad crew
stories.text: Half the pad crew is down with influenza. The other half can prepare one launch, carefully.

stories.headline: Hardware grounded pending checks
stories.text: A defect found in one part may run through several of the agency's designs. They are grounded until every unit has been inspected.

stories.headline: A strike at the supplier
stories.text: Workers at a key supplier walk out. Without its parts, several of the agency's designs cannot be built for a while.

stories.headline: The warehouse floods
stories.text: A burst main floods the parts warehouse. Several designs wait until replacements are made and certified.

stories.headline: The {group} take the blame
stories.text: After the failure, the papers point at the {group}. Some of them stop answering the phone at home.

stories.headline: An inquiry hangs over the {group}
stories.text: Investigators interview the {group} one by one about the failure. Nobody knows who will be held responsible.

stories.headline: Sleepless nights for the {group}
stories.text: The {group} replay the failure over and over. The corridors are quiet, and the canteen half empty.

stories.headline: The pads need repairs
stories.text: Inspectors find cracked concrete in the flame trenches. No launches until the pads are rebuilt.

stories.headline: A storm shuts the site
stories.text: A violent storm tears down power lines and floods the access roads. The launch site is closed for the turn.

stories.headline: Launches suspended by order
stories.text: With delicate talks under way abroad, the government orders all launches put off until they are over.

stories.headline: {name} killed in a training jet
stories.text: {name}'s jet trainer crashes on a routine proficiency flight. The agency flies its flags at half mast.

stories.headline: {name} dies in a test chamber fire
stories.text: A fire breaks out in a pressure chamber during a ground test. {name} cannot be reached in time.

stories.headline: {name} lost in a parachute jump
stories.text: {name}'s parachute fails to open on a training jump. The whole corps attends the funeral.

stories.headline: A spending scandal
stories.text: A newspaper reveals that an agency official furnished an office at public expense. The story runs for a week.

stories.headline: Neighbours complain
stories.text: Towns near the test stands complain of broken windows and sleepless nights. The agency is in every local paper, for the wrong reasons.

stories.headline: A critical book
stories.text: A popular book argues the space programme is money better spent at home. It is the season's bestseller.

stories.headline: A supplier goes bankrupt
stories.text: The firm that made the agency's precision instruments goes bankrupt. Engineers spend their days finding and checking new sources.

stories.headline: The computer breaks down
stories.text: The agency's only large computer burns out a bank of valves. Calculations go back to slide rules until it is repaired.

stories.headline: A reorganisation
stories.text: A new management structure moves departments and changes who signs what. For a while, nobody quite knows whom to ask.

stories.headline: A test stand is damaged
stories.text: An engine shuts down badly and damages the test stand's frame. It has to be rebuilt before the next firing.

stories.headline: A lawsuit is settled
stories.text: A farmer whose cattle stampeded at an engine test sues the agency. The lawyers advise settling, and the agency pays.

stories.headline: Material prices jump
stories.text: The price of titanium and special steels jumps overnight. The agency pays the difference on contracts already signed.

stories.headline: An explosion at the fuel depot
stories.text: A fuel depot explodes during a transfer. The repairs are expensive, and no rocket leaves the site until the depot is safe.

stories.headline: Fire in the control building
stories.text: An electrical fire guts part of the launch control building. The rewiring costs dearly, and no launch can go this turn.

stories.headline: A service tower collapses
stories.text: High winds bring down a service tower onto the pad. Clearing and rebuilding is costly, and launches wait.
